## Outline

1.  Model assumptions, simulations, and diagnostics
2.  Practice

# Model assumptions

## Overview

Linear regression assumes:

-   **Linearity** — the relationship between predictors and response is linear
-   **Independence** — errors are independent of each other
-   **Homoscedasticity** — constant error variance
-   **Normality** — residuals are normally distributed

::: callout-note
Assumptions are often violated by real data. Here we simulate violations and learn to detect and address them.
:::

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
rm(list = ls())
library(stats)
library(nlme)
library(splines)
```
:::


## When assumptions are met


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y <- 50 + 3 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 4)
plot(y ~ x)
```
:::


## Diagnostics: met assumptions


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x    <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y    <- 50 + 3 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 4)
my_lm <- lm(y ~ x)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(my_lm)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


## Predictions: met assumptions


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x    <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y    <- 50 + 3 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 4)
my_lm <- lm(y ~ x)

prediction <- data.frame(x = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100))
prediction$fit <- predict(my_lm, newdata = prediction)

plot(y ~ x)
lines(fit ~ x, prediction, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
:::


## Violating linearity: simulate


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y <- 50 + 3 * x - 0.5 * x^2 + rnorm(length(x), 0, 2)
plot(y ~ x)
```
:::


## Violating linearity: diagnostics


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x     <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y     <- 50 + 3 * x - 0.5 * x^2 + rnorm(length(x), 0, 2)
my_lm <- lm(y ~ x)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(my_lm)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


## Fix: polynomial term


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x     <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y     <- 50 + 3 * x - 0.5 * x^2 + rnorm(length(x), 0, 2)
my_lm <- lm(y ~ x + I(x^2))    # include quadratic term

prediction      <- data.frame(x = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100))
prediction$fit  <- predict(my_lm, newdata = prediction)

plot(y ~ x)
lines(fit ~ x, prediction, col = "red", lwd = 2)
```
:::


## Violating homoscedasticity


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x     <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y     <- 1.5 + 0.75 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 0.15 * x)
my_lm <- lm(y ~ x)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(my_lm)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


## Fix: GLS with variance structure


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x      <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y      <- 1.5 + 0.75 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 0.15 * x)
my_gls <- nlme::gls(y ~ x, weights = nlme::varFixed(~x))

# Predictions using delta method from vcov()
new_data       <- data.frame(x = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100))
X_mat          <- model.matrix(~ x, data = new_data)
new_data$fit   <- as.numeric(X_mat %*% coef(my_gls))
vcov_mat       <- vcov(my_gls)
se_pred        <- sqrt(diag(X_mat %*% vcov_mat %*% t(X_mat)))
new_data$uci   <- new_data$fit + 1.96 * se_pred
new_data$lci   <- new_data$fit - 1.96 * se_pred

plot(y ~ x)
lines(fit ~ x, new_data, col = "red",    lwd = 2)
lines(uci ~ x, new_data, col = "red",    lwd = 1, lty = 2)
lines(lci ~ x, new_data, col = "red",    lwd = 1, lty = 2)
```
:::


## Violating normality


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(541)
x     <- runif(200, 5, 15)
y     <- log(1.5 + 1 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 2))
my_lm <- lm(y ~ x)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(my_lm)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


::: callout-tip
Can you think of a solution from a previous lesson? (Hint: link functions)
:::

## Outliers: simulate


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
set.seed(123)
x <- sample(2:5, 10, replace = TRUE)
set.seed(124)
y <- 1.5 - 0.1 * x + rnorm(length(x), 0, 1)

# Add one outlier
y <- c(10, y)
x <- c(1,  x)

my_lm <- lm(y ~ x)
plot(y ~ x)
abline(my_lm, col = "red")
```
:::


## Outlier diagnostics


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(my_lm)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


# Practice

## Practice 1: simulations

::: {.callout-tip title="Practice 1"}
1.  Use `ns()` from the `splines` package to fit a model with a non-linear relationship.
2.  Simulate **decreasing** residual variance with increasing x. Plot to confirm.
3.  Plot residual density vs. a normal curve for the normality-violating data. Suggest a model fix.
4.  Remove the outlier and re-run diagnostics. Does it change conclusions?
:::


::: {.cell}

```{.webr .cell-code}
library(splines)
# Spline-based fit
set.seed(541)
x     <- runif(200, 1, 10)
y     <- 50 + 3 * x - 0.5 * x^2 + rnorm(length(x), 0, 2)
my_ns <- lm(y ~ ns(x, df = 3))

prediction     <- data.frame(x = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 100))
prediction$fit <- predict(my_ns, newdata = prediction)
plot(y ~ x)
lines(fit ~ x, prediction, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
```
:::


## Practice 2: your data

::: {.callout-tip title="Practice 2"}
1.  Run `plot(lm(...))` on a linear regression model for your own data.
2.  Which assumptions, if any, appear to be violated?
3.  Demonstrate how you would address the violation(s).
:::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
